competences: The learner names decentralised sectors and explains their importance.
The learner identifies duties and challenges of local government leaders.
languageCompetence: Learners pronounce, read and spell decentralisation, local council, government sector, administration and expenditure.
objectives: By the end of the period, learners should name three decentralised sectors in Uganda.
By the end of the period, learners should answer sourced questions on the contributions and challenges of district leaders.
priorKnowledge: Learners learnt the meaning, government levels and advantages of decentralisation in the preceding lesson.
materials: P4 SST notes on decentralisation and district leadership
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the earlier lesson on decentralisation and asks "Give any one way decentralisation affects the development of the country.". They identify what learners remember about local government and its advantages before starting a continuation exercise.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall their previous decentralisation notes, answer the introductory question and state a benefit for the local community.

steps.content: Primary health care is a decentralised sector. Primary education is a decentralised sector. Agriculture is a decentralised sector. Local leaders settle community disputes. Local councils maintain law and order. Local leaders implement government policies. Decentralisation can increase government expenditure. Equal provision of services can become difficult.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the listed facts about decentralised services, including "Primary health care is a decentralised sector." and "Primary education is a decentralised sector.". They explain local leaders' duties using the original examples and ask "Give any three ways leaders are important in the society." and "Give any three ways leaders are important in the community.".
steps.learnerActivity: Learners name decentralised sectors, explain local leadership duties and copy the eight revision points into their books before practice.

steps.content: Give any one way decentralisation affects the development of the country. | Give any three ways leaders are important in the society. | Give any three ways leaders are important in the community. | State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties. | Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced questions from the book, beginning with "State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties." and "Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village.". They supervise individual answers, then compare responses with documented community duties and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners attempt the source questions independently, check the responses against the revised points and make corrections on their written work.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the decentralised sectors and uses "Give any one way decentralisation affects the development of the country." to check understanding. They assign the remaining sourced exercise questions without inventing further examples or homework.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners share a correct point about decentralisation, answer the final oral question and record the homework in their books.

assessment: Ask "Give any one way decentralisation affects the development of the country.", "Give any three ways leaders are important in the society.", and "State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties.". Mark learners' answers from the supplied lesson notes.
homework: Complete the sourced question: "Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village."
